source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's NYM7 campus in Wappingers Falls publishes 3 MW of IT capacity and 100,000 square feet of technical space, making it the only facility in New York with a published megawatt figure.

That single figure is the entire published capacity total for the state, out of 31 mapped facilities. The gap between 31 mapped sites and one disclosed number is the real finding: New York's data center footprint is documented far more thoroughly than its power draw. A 3 MW campus is small against the densities AI training clusters now demand, and the arithmetic at 40 kW per rack puts it near 75 racks, though the operator publishes no rack count to confirm it.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers audited controls for hosting services and says nothing about AI workloads. Nothing published here addresses liquid cooling, high-density power delivery, or substation and interconnection arrangements, which are the factors that would decide whether accelerators could run at the site. On the published record this is general colocation, and any AI use of it is undocumented.

What the data does not cover is most of what matters for the compute thesis. There is no tenant list, no accelerator count, no announced expansion, and no grid or interconnection detail. The 3 MW figure describes disclosed capacity, not built capacity, and the state ranking it produces reflects how little operators publish rather than how much infrastructure exists.
